premise: A decision made on missing information is a guess wearing a suit. Each entry states what is known, what is not, why it blocks a decision, and the cheapest concrete action that would answer it. Q-22 and Q-23 were added 2026-11-20 by session ce911db5; the account-status question had been described in DIRECTION.md but never registered (FLG-028).

status_scale.blocking: A decision is on hold until this is answered.
status_scale.queued: Should be answered before the next content release.
status_scale.watch: Will answer itself once the site has traffic; revisit then.
status_scale.owner-only: Cannot be answered from outside the owner's accounts.

questions.question: Is this one publication about cooking to a target temperature, or two sites — air fryers and thermometers?
questions.blocks: Every content, navigation and brand decision that follows.
questions.known: The five products are three air fryers and two thermometers across four brands (S10-S14). The current site treats "food hot, then food proven done" as the unifying beat.
questions.unknown: Whether the owner intends to sell more of one family than the other, which would settle it commercially rather than editorially.
questions.how_to_find_out: Look at the Associates dashboard's ordered-items report after 30 days of traffic. If one family produces under 10% of orders, narrow.
questions.changes: Whether the site keeps two category hubs or collapses to one.

questions.question: Do the five Special Links actually carry tag=shopnow047c-20?
questions.blocks: Any claim that the site earns anything. If the tag is missing, clicks earn nothing.
questions.known: The 2026-11-19 observation records each supplied short link reaching one of five ASINs (S10-S14). The resolved URLs carried query parameters but no visible tag= value in what was served to that session (F-09, FLG-031).
questions.unknown: Whether the Associates ID is attached server-side, which is invisible from outside the account.
questions.how_to_find_out: Sign in to Associates, open a product page with SiteStripe active, and read the Get Link panel for one of the five. Confirm the tag field. Then make one test click and confirm it appears in the Click Reports within 24 hours.
questions.changes: If the tag is absent, every outbound link needs regenerating before any traffic is worth attracting.

questions.question: What commission rate applies to each of the five products, under the account's current rate card?
questions.blocks: Any prioritisation of one product over another. Without it, "which product should the site push" has no answer.
questions.known: The Commission Income Statement is published as part of the Associates Program Policies and sets rates by product category; it can change (S02).
questions.unknown: The applicable rate for Kitchen & Dining small appliances as it applies to this account today. That figure is account-specific and was not available to this session.
questions.how_to_find_out: Read the current Commission Income Statement in the Associates dashboard and record the fixed and variable rates for the categories the five ASINs sit in.
questions.changes: Whether the air fryers or the thermometers get the prime navigation slot, and whether the layout should favour the higher-ticket item.

questions.question: Is the link.amazon short-link format acceptable in this account's enrolled workflow?
questions.blocks: Whether the supplied links can ever be the published destination.
questions.known: Program Policies 6(w) prohibits a shortening service used so that it is unclear the link goes to an Amazon Site (S02; clause read and quoted 2026-11-20). The site currently publishes direct amazon.com/dp/ URLs, so clarity is not in question there.
questions.unknown: Whether these particular links resolve visibly and are accepted in the enrolled workflow. Their compliance status is not established either way — nothing here calls them invalid (F-13).
questions.how_to_find_out: Run SG-13: click one link while signed in, confirm the destination and confirm the click is reported. Repeat if it passes.
questions.changes: Whether short links can appear anywhere user-facing, or stay as a provenance record only.

questions.question: Who is the named author, and what is their actual experience?
questions.blocks: Any byline, any "about" page, and any statement of expertise. Right now authorship is stated as what it is — an editorial desk with no hands-on testing.
questions.known: Google's guidance asks who created the content and rewards demonstrated experience (S21). The FTC prohibits claiming experience you do not have (S03).
questions.unknown: The owner's real name, whether they have used any of these appliances, and whether they are willing to be named.
questions.how_to_find_out: The owner decides: either publish a named author with a truthful one-paragraph background, or keep the desk byline and accept slower trust-building.
questions.changes: Every byline, the about page, and whether the site can ever use an experience-led voice.

questions.question: Will the site ever buy or receive units to test?
questions.blocks: The highest-value article type in this niche — what the appliance is like to live with.
questions.known: No unit has been handled (C-07), so no such page can be written honestly today (S22). SG-06 sets out the three options.
questions.unknown: Whether there is a budget for one unit per family, and whether the owner would accept gifted units with disclosure.
questions.how_to_find_out: Set a rule before the first offer arrives: buy everything, or accept gifts only with a visible line on the page, or decline.
questions.cost: the price of one air fryer and one thermometer
questions.changes: Whether the content plan stays specification-led indefinitely.

questions.question: Which analytics will actually be installed, given no cookies and no personal data?
questions.blocks: Choosing the next article and knowing whether the published guides worked.
questions.known: No analytics endpoint and no Search Console property exist (F-17). The site ships a cookie-free, network-free client-side counter (SG-08).
questions.unknown: Whether the owner has hosting that can run a small endpoint, and whether they want one at all.
questions.how_to_find_out: Decide between: Search Console only (zero cost, query data, no page-level behaviour); a self-hosted endpoint (needs a host); or nothing.
questions.cost: Search Console is free; a self-hosted endpoint needs a small host
questions.changes: Whether traffic can be measured at all, and therefore whether the content plan can ever be data-driven.

questions.question: What counts as "a session" for the site's own ledger?
questions.blocks: Any session-based metric. Two people counting sessions differently produce two different conversion rates from the same clicks.
questions.known: Amazon defines a Session precisely for its own attribution: it begins at the click and ends at 24 hours, an order, or another Special Link click (S02).
questions.unknown: Whether the site's own ledger should mirror Amazon's definition or use a page-view-based one.
questions.how_to_find_out: Adopt Amazon's definition verbatim for any column that will be reconciled against Associates reporting; use a separate, clearly named column otherwise.
questions.changes: The column definitions in the campaign ledger.

questions.question: What is the target outcome for the first 90 days?
questions.blocks: Whether effort should go into more articles, more products, or better conversion on the five that exist.
questions.known: There is no traffic and no revenue yet (F-10). Every current number on the site is a specification, not a performance figure.
questions.unknown: Whether the owner wants clicks, orders, or simply a credible site that exists.
questions.how_to_find_out: Write the number down before looking at any dashboard. "First order" and "first 100 clicks" imply very different content plans.
questions.changes: The entire content calendar from the next guide onward.

questions.question: Should P4 point at the newer ASIN the listing itself recommends?
questions.blocks: Whether the site sends readers to a superseded model.
questions.known: The P-04 listing displays "There is a newer model of this item" and links ASIN B0GL7Z4KP4 (S13). The supplied short link resolves to B0DHZTCNR5 (F-03).
questions.unknown: Whether the owner deliberately chose the older ASIN, or supplied a stale link.
questions.how_to_find_out: Compare the two listings directly and decide. If the newer one is chosen, update intended.asin and record the change with a date — never edit observed.
questions.changes: One outbound link and one product page.

questions.question: What is the real capacity of P1 in litres?
questions.blocks: Any capacity-per-counter-centimetre comparison involving P1.
questions.known: The listing says 6 liters in one field and 6 quarts in the title; the two do not agree (F-01).
questions.unknown: Whether the baskets hold 6 US quarts (about 5.68 L) or 6 L total.
questions.how_to_find_out: Ask the manufacturer, or measure a unit. Until then, publish the nominal figure with the conflict named, as the site does now.
questions.changes: One row of the footprint analysis.

questions.question: Is the brand name and visual direction settled?
questions.blocks: A logo, a domain, and any consistency beyond the current typographic treatment.
questions.known: The site currently uses a working name and a type-led visual system with no logo and no product photography (F-19).
questions.unknown: Whether the owner wants a brand at all, or prefers the neutral publication look.
questions.how_to_find_out: Decide the name first, because it constrains the domain, which constrains the canonical URLs. Changing it later means changing every canonical, the sitemap and the feed together.
questions.changes: Every canonical URL, the sitemap, the feed, and the site's manifest.

questions.question: If a self-hosted analytics endpoint is added, what exactly will it store?
questions.blocks: Whether any server-side measurement is permitted at all.
questions.known: Program Policies 2(b) forbids associating a sub-tag or ID with an individual user (S02). Any endpoint storing IP addresses or setting cookies creates exactly that association.
questions.unknown: What the owner's host logs by default — most log IP addresses unless told not to.
questions.how_to_find_out: Write the retention rule first: path, product id, timestamp, nothing else; no cookies; IP discarded before write. Then configure the host to match.
questions.changes: Whether SG-08 ever moves from a browser counter to a real denominator.

questions.question: What is the publishing cadence, and who writes the next guide?
questions.blocks: Whether the site keeps the cadence it has written down.
questions.known: The published guides live in articles/*.html. A monthly cadence with a next-due date and an approver is written down in docs/publishing-cadence.md (decision DT-10); nothing in the repository publishes automatically.
questions.unknown: Whether the owner writes, or the agent drafts for approval, and how often.
questions.how_to_find_out: Pick a cadence the owner will actually keep — one a fortnight beats three a week followed by silence. Write it in the repository so the next session honours it.
questions.changes: The editorial calendar and the build's release checklist.

questions.question: Does the disclosure placement satisfy the standard if a reader never scrolls?
questions.blocks: Nothing — but it should be re-checked, not assumed.
questions.known: The disclosure sits in a strip immediately under the masthead, above the first heading, on every page, and again in the footer (C-01, C-02). The FTC test is that it is hard to miss and placed with the endorsement (S03).
questions.unknown: How the strip renders on a narrow screen with a large system font size, which is the case where "above the fold" gets squeezed.
questions.how_to_find_out: Open any page at 320 px width with text scaled up and confirm the disclosure is still visible before the first product button.
questions.verification_2026-11-19: Structural check passes and is enforced by a gate: tools/check_site.py P01-disclosure-position fails any page where the disclosure marker does not appear before the first <h1>, so on every one of the 21 pages the disclosure precedes all headings and product content in reading order. The strip is a normal full-width block (not positioned after the hero), so it is not reordered below content at 320px. The mobile-first pass (S-20, session 65474d4f) also sets the strip to 0.8rem at <=600px so it stays compact rather than pushing content. A physical pixel measurement in a real browser at 320px with an enlarged system font was NOT run from this sandbox; that last confirmation remains a browser task.
questions.changes: The masthead layout, if the strip wraps below the fold.

questions.question: Is a custom domain worth it, and if so which one?
questions.blocks: Nothing today; it matters more as soon as the URL has to be said out loud or printed anywhere.
questions.known: The site is on a project path under a shared GitHub Pages hostname (F-16). Every canonical, sitemap entry and feed URL is absolute and would all change together.
questions.unknown: Whether the owner owns a domain, and whether the brand name in Q-12 will change.
questions.how_to_find_out: Answer Q-12 first, then decide the domain. Note that a domain must not contain an Amazon trademark or a variant of one (S02).
questions.changes: Every absolute URL on the site.

questions.question: Which of the published guides should be retired if Search Console shows no impressions after 60 days?
questions.blocks: Nothing yet. It is the question that stops a site accumulating pages nobody reads.
questions.known: The published guides live in articles/*.html, and no impression or query data exists yet (F-17).
questions.unknown: Which pages, if any, will fail to earn an impression. That number cannot be guessed.
questions.how_to_find_out: After 60 days, sort the Pages report by impressions. Any page with zero impressions earns a rewrite, a merge, or a removal — decided with data, not taste.
questions.changes: The shape of the article set.

questions.question: Does the owner have Search Console access for this GitHub Pages site, and will they verify it this month?
questions.blocks: Every measured-topic decision (SG-07, SG-18, Q-17).
questions.known: The site emits sitemap.xml and robots.txt pointing at it; verification is an account action, not a code action.
questions.unknown: Whether anyone will actually open the property. Without it the site publishes blind.
questions.how_to_find_out: Owner adds the property in Search Console, verifies via DNS or file upload, submits sitemap.xml, and reports back. Ten minutes, once.
questions.changes: Whether the next topic is measured or guessed.

questions.question: Is the Associates account eligible for Product Advertising API access today?
questions.blocks: Any future price display (SG-17) and any automation that reads live listing data.
questions.known: PA-API eligibility depends on account standing and qualifying sales, visible only inside the account.
questions.unknown: Whether the account has ever generated the sales required.
questions.how_to_find_out: Associates Central → Account Settings → Product Advertising API. If the tab is missing, the account is not yet eligible; record the date checked.
questions.changes: Whether prices can ever appear on this site.

questions.question: Which email provider, consent language, and retention period will the owner accept for reader capture?
questions.blocks: FLG-014 / reader_signup staying a reserved event; any return-visit channel other than RSS.
questions.known: The demo form was removed because it faked a confirmation. No provider, endpoint, or consent copy exists.
questions.unknown: Which provider the owner will pay for and what their consent text must say.
questions.how_to_find_out: Owner picks a provider (or declines); editorial drafts the consent line and privacy note; the form ships only after the endpoint responds. analytics.html gets an update in the same commit.
questions.changes: A second audience channel, or continued RSS-only.

questions.question: Does the og-image render in the share previewers the site cares about?
questions.blocks: Nothing; it is a quality-of-preview question with a cheap answer.
questions.known: The markup now references assets/og-image.png (a 1200×630 raster card) on every page; the SVG reference was replaced after F-21 was raised. F-21 records the remaining unverified step.
questions.unknown: Whether Facebook, X, LinkedIn, or messaging apps draw the card from an SVG reference.
questions.how_to_find_out: Run any public share debugger on the live URL and screenshot the result. The PNG per SG-16 is already shipped; this run only confirms the card renders.
questions.changes: Whether shared links show a card at all.

questions.question: Why do the supplied short links sometimes end at the Amazon homepage instead of a product page?
questions.blocks: Whether any buy button can be attributed at all when its destination varies within a day, and which links a fresh Special Link should replace.
questions.known: On 2026-11-19 all five ended at a product page. Six dated passes on 2026-11-20 disagree and all are kept: (1) an earlier session (data/products.json, live_recheck_2026_11_20) — B04G1MEwY ended at https://www.amazon.com/ twice, the other four ended at their product pages; (2) session arena/ce911db5-prod3 — B0c8moW59 ended at https://www.amazon.com/ twice (kept on FLG-031, this row and the coordination board); (3) session arena/6bf60cac-prod3 (live_recheck_2026_11_20_link_check) — all five ended at the homepage (FLG-025); (4) session arena/6c0972fb-prod3 recorded the same independently for all five (FLG-039); (5) session arena/d52ad947-prod3 again recorded the homepage for B04G1MEwY and B0c8moW59; (6) session arena/74e655e9-prod3 (live_recheck_2026_11_20_session_74e655e9) — B04G1MEwY reached its product page twice, B0c8moW59 reached its product page after an HTTP 500, and B0f3GKalj reached its product page, while B02NbDxp3 and B00hJ57DV ended at the homepage; no final URL in pass 6 carried tag=shopnow047c-20. Nothing is deleted and no tie is broken.
questions.unknown: Whether the cause is link expiry, a signed-out fetch versus an enrolled account, a profile gate or a transient response. None can be distinguished from outside the account, so none is asserted.
questions.how_to_find_out: Signed in, open each of the five links once. Note the final URL, whether it lands on the product or the homepage, and whether it carries tag=shopnow047c-20. Then check Link Reports for a same-day click. If a link still lands on the homepage there, regenerate that Special Link from the product page with SiteStripe and record the new URL.
questions.changes: Whether the homepage-reaching buy buttons are replaced with freshly generated Special Links, or kept as supplied.

questions.question: Is tracking ID shopnow047c-20 attached to an enrolled, currently eligible Amazon Associates account?
questions.blocks: Every claim that the site can earn anything, and whether the disclosure describes a current relationship or a possible one.
questions.known: The tracking ID was supplied by the owner. The site states the required sentence and adds conditional wording; it never asserts current enrollment or income.
questions.unknown: Whether the account exists, is enrolled, is in good standing and meets the program's qualification requirements. None of it is readable from outside the account.
questions.how_to_find_out: Associates Central: read Account Settings for the tracking ID and status, and the account/payment page for standing. Record the date and what the screen said. If the ID is not there, the disclosure and every link assumption need correcting before any promotion.
questions.changes: Whether the site describes a live affiliate relationship or a prospective one.

questions.question: Does the link.amazon redirect attach tag=shopnow047c-20 to the destination URL?
questions.blocks: Whether the five buy links can be credited at all. Every earning claim depends on it.
questions.known: Program Policies §2(b) require the tag as a parameter in the URL of each link to an Amazon Site. None of the 23 shipped link.amazon anchors and none of 192 amazon.com anchors contain a tag parameter (FLG-026).
questions.unknown: Whether the short-link service appends the tag during the redirect. This is not visible from a plain fetch, because the fetch follows to a page that does not display the referrer's tag.
questions.how_to_find_out: Signed in to Associates, click one supplied link once in a normal browser. In the Associates report, check that the click appears within the reporting window, then open the same link with the redirect chain visible (browser dev tools → Network → preserve log) and read whether tag= appears on the amazon.com URL.
questions.changes: Whether the buy buttons can stay pointed at the supplied short links or must be replaced with freshly generated Special Links (DT-01).

questions.question: Why did all five supplied links end at the Amazon homepage on the third check, when four of five reached product pages earlier the same day?
questions.blocks: Nothing structurally, but it decides whether the buy buttons should keep pointing at the short links.
questions.known: Four dated observations exist: 2026-11-19 all five reached product pages; 2026-11-20 session 70e8475c one of five reached the homepage; session ce911db5 two of five; session 6bf60cac all five (FLG-017, FLG-031, FLG-025). No record is overwritten.
questions.unknown: Whether the change is geographic, time-of-day, a per-fetch rate limit, a change on Amazon's side, or something about the fetching client. No logs are available to the site.
questions.how_to_find_out: Owner clicks all five while signed in, at three times of day, and records the landing page each time. Comparing those with the site's records is the only test that separates a link problem from a fetch-method problem.
questions.changes: Whether the site describes the supplied links as working, unresolved, or in need of replacement.

questions.question: Who signs off the twelve-week plan, and what happens to a row whose evidence never arrives?
questions.blocks: The publishing cadence, and whether the plan page stays honest as weeks pass.
questions.known: Twelve rows are proposed in data/editorial-plan.json with dated calendar hooks; four are partly or wholly blocked on a figure no source publishes.
questions.unknown: Whether the owner wants a blocked row dropped, replaced, or held in place with its gap named. Each choice produces a different page.
questions.how_to_find_out: A decision on the plan page itself: mark each row Do this / Maybe / No (the same control the ideas register uses), and record the choice.
questions.changes: Whether the plan page describes proposals or commitments.

questions.question: Which of the trend-led article topics earns impressions, and should the next guide be one of them?
questions.blocks: Choosing the next article from measured demand (SG-18, SG-37); depends on Q-18 first.
questions.known: No Search Console impressions or query data exist yet (F-17). Q-18 must be answered before any topic can be chosen from data.
questions.unknown: Which question clusters around air fryers and meat thermometers actually bring qualified visitors, and whether a seasonal topic or a specification topic wins.
questions.how_to_find_out: After Q-18 is answered (Search Console verified and sitemap submitted), review the Queries report after enough data accrues, pick a cluster with impressions and no dedicated page, and write the next guide around it.
questions.changes: The topic and timing of the next guide.

questions.question: Is any of this site in Google's index yet, and which pages?
questions.blocks: Judging whether any guide is discoverable at all; choosing between publishing more (SG-18's pipeline) and fixing discoverability first. Until this is answered, any statement about organic traffic is a guess.
questions.known: The site ships unique canonicals, a robots.txt pointing at sitemap.xml, a sitemap and an RSS feed — all enforced by the repo's gates. Coordination records show GitHub Pages deployments since 2026-11-19.
questions.unknown: Whether Google has crawled or indexed any URL; which pages, if any, appear for brand or topic queries. Nothing hosted on the site itself can answer this.
questions.how_to_find_out: Two steps. (1) Public, no account: a site:wingbangboozle1-lang.github.io/Prod3 query — a rough, incomplete indication; record the date and the result count, not a claim of completeness. (2) Authoritative: Search Console → property → Pages report, after Q-18's verification — it lists indexed and excluded URLs with reasons (S26).
questions.changes: Whether “publish and wait” is a plan or a hope, and whether the next guide should be written at all before indexing is confirmed.

questions.question: What do Core Web Vitals measure on this site today, on a mid-range phone?
questions.blocks: SG-46 (the proposed CWV gate) and any decision to add visual effects; until measured, the mobile-first and light-page claims (S-20 pass) are design statements, not records.
questions.known: The stylesheet is one local file with system fonts (no webfonts, no @import), pages load one local script each, and there are no third-party asset requests on shop pages — verified by a URL scan on 2026-11-20 (T-54 log). Tap targets were audited at 48px (S-20).
questions.unknown: LCP, INP and CLS as actually measured. No dated lab or field result exists anywhere in the repository.
questions.how_to_find_out: pagespeed.web.dev — enter the live URL, choose mobile, and record the dated metric values on analytics.html; Lighthouse in Chrome gives the same lab metrics. No account is required.
questions.changes: Turns “the site is light” from a design claim into a dated measurement, and sets the baseline that SG-46's gate would compare future changes against.

questions.question: Do the outbound-click counters fire on the tagged product buttons, and where do the counts land?
questions.blocks: SG-48, and any statement about which button gets clicked. The campaign ledger stays empty until an authorized first-party report exists.
questions.known: assets/app.js records a click event per outbound link with an ASIN label; scripts/check_site.py rule 7b now counts the tagged buttons (30 on 2026-11-20), so the population being measured is known and stable. The event has a data-event name and a data-asin, both machine-checkable.
questions.unknown: Whether anything receives or stores the event. No analytics endpoint is configured (DT-07), and no first-party report exists, so no click count, conversion rate or revenue figure can be quoted anywhere on this site.
questions.how_to_find_out: Owner: decide DT-07 (self-hosted counter, a privacy-preserving hosted endpoint, or nothing). If nothing is chosen, the local-only counts and this question should be closed as won't-measure, and the ledger's columns stay defined but empty.

questions.question: Does a tag added to a product URL outside Associates Central credit this account, and does the click show up in the reports?
questions.blocks: Whether the tagging shipped on 2026-11-20 is the final answer or a placeholder for links generated inside the account (Q-02, Q-24, FLG-039).
questions.known: Participation Requirements 2(b) prescribes the tag as a URL parameter and states that Special Links “may be created by you or made available to you by us”, so a self-built tagged link is a permitted format. Every product link on this site now carries ?tag=shopnow047c-20 (369 anchors), and gate D41 fails the build if one does not (FLG-026).
questions.unknown: Whether the tracking ID sits on an enrolled, eligible account; whether this account credits a manually tagged link; whether the reported click count moves after a test click. Commission Income Statement 2(g) is why the cost of not checking is lost earnings rather than a visible break.
questions.how_to_find_out: Associates Central → Link Checker: paste one tagged product URL from the live site and confirm the tool reports this tracking ID — Amazon documents the tool for links “created or modified on your own outside of Associates Central” (S40). Then open the live page, click while signed in, and read the click report the next day. Record both dates here; the same pass answers Q-02 and Q-24.
questions.changes: Whether the five product paths stay as tagged listing URLs or are replaced by links generated in the account.
questions.note: Added 2026-11-20 by session 52f418e7. Drafted as Q-28, then Q-30; both numbers were taken upstream while this branch was in flight, so this row moved twice and nothing else was renumbered.

sources_note: Each question carries the registered source IDs of the official document that speaks to it, or an empty list plus evidence_status='unverified' when no official document settles it. Nothing is cited that does not answer the question.
